nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a finite graph and $s$ a natural number. For an $(s+1)$-arc $\gamma = (x_0, \dots, x_{s+1})$ of $X$, its *head* is the $s$-arc $(x_1, \dots, x_{s+1})$ and its *tail* is the $s$-arc $(x_0, \dots, x_s)$. If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are $s$-arcs of $X$, then $\beta$ *follows* $\alpha$ if there is an $(s+1)$-arc of $X$ whose tail is $\alpha$ and whose head is $\beta$. nodes.title: $s$-arc digraph

nodes.summary: A finite graph $G$ is $s$-arc regular if it has at least one $s$-arc and, for any two $s$-arcs $(u_0, \dots, u_s)$ and $(v_0, \dots, v_s)$ of $G$, there is exactly one automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$ with $\varphi(u_i) = v_i$ for every $i \le s$.
nodes.title: $s$-arc regular graph

nodes.summary: A finite graph $G$ is $s$-arc transitive if its automorphism group acts transitively on its $s$-arcs: for any two $s$-arcs $(u_0, \dots, u_s)$ and $(v_0, \dots, v_s)$ of $G$ there is an automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$ with $\varphi(u_i) = v_i$ for every $i \le s$.
nodes.title: $s$-arc transitive graph

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a finite graph and $s$ a natural number. An *$s$-arc* in $X$ is a sequence $(v_0, \dots, v_s)$ of vertices of $X$ such that $v_{i-1}$ and $v_i$ are adjacent for $1 \le i \le s$, and $v_{i-1} \ne v_{i+1}$ for $0 < i < s$.
nodes.title: $s$-arc

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
